newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia orders kids indoors to avoid killer virus.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia orders kids indoors to avoid killer virus.

text.p: Malaysia has asked parents all over the country to keep children indoors as a deadly strain of Coxsackie B virus in eastern state of Sarawak claimed its 25th victim, newspapers said on Saturday.
They quoted Health Minister Chua Jui Meng as saying parents should keep children below the age of two inside to avoid exposure to the killer virus.

"We estimated that there are about 40,000 children below two in Sarawak and our advice is for them to stay indoors to avoid contact with those who may be infected," Chua told reporters at a hospital in Sibu in Sarawak state.
"It's better to be safe than sorry," he said.
All the victims of the virus, which was detected on April 14, have been young children, 19 of them below two years of age. The latest was a 22-month-old boy.
In Kuala Lumpur, 20 children were hospitalised with "hand-foot-mouth" disease, but doctors were not sure if they were also infected by Coxsackie virus, the newspapers said.

The symptoms of the children infected in Kuala Lumpur were similar to those affected by Coxsackie B virus, Mohamed Sham Kassim, chief paediatrician at Kuala Lumpur General Hospital, was quoted as saying by the New Straits Times.
In Sarawak, 118 infants were still being warded for the infection, Health Minister Chua said.
He said there had been 334 admissions into Sarawak hospitals since the outbreak, of which 216 have been discharged.
Experts from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta are in Malaysia trying to determine the nature of the infection.
The virus was originally found in infected food but can be airborne, health officials said. Symptoms include fever, nervous fits and paralysis and could lead to heart failure.
